summary: Dedicated burst limit updated in control plane but Console shows stale limit value (propagation/cache delay)
body:
Customer (Northpeak Search) reports that after Redwood Support adjusted their tenant burst limit, the Dedicated Console still shows the previous limit value.

Issue summary
- Tenant: northpeak-prod (Dedicated, eu-west)
- What changed: burst.max_gpu_ratio and burst.max_burst_gpus were increased via control plane admin tooling.
- Expected: Console "Burst capacity" panel updates within a few minutes.
- Actual: Console continued to display the old limit for ~45 minutes; API behavior appeared to follow the new limit (fewer 429s at previous cap).

Customer impact
- Customer confusion during a planned indexing run; they were trying to verify the new cap before starting the job.
- No production outage; burst admission and metering appeared correct.

Environment
- Console: prod
- Region: eu-west

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Update burst limits for a tenant via control plane admin endpoint.
2) Immediately open Console -> Dedicated -> Burst capacity.
3) Observe limit values sometimes remain stale even though the underlying control plane read API returns the new config.

Initial hypotheses
- Console backend caching tenant config too aggressively (Redis + in-process cache) and not invalidating on writes.
- CDN caching on the Console BFF endpoint.
- Read replica lag for the tenant config store (write goes to primary; Console reads from replica).

Evidence collected
- At 2025-06-10 16:18 UTC, control plane read API (/v1/tenants/{id}/burst-config) returned the updated values.
- Console BFF endpoint continued returning the previous values until 2025-06-10 17:03 UTC.
- Console UI was not hard-refreshing the limit state when the page was already open (customer had the page open before the change).

Acceptance criteria for fix
- Post-change, Console reflects updated burst config within 5 minutes (p95).
- If values are older than 5 minutes, Console should display a "Refreshing…" indicator or surface last-updated timestamp.
- Ensure change events are audit logged (already required) and can be used for invalidation hooks.

Customer-facing note (what we told them)
- The burst limit change is active immediately in the control plane; Console display can lag due to caching.
- As a workaround, hard refresh and/or wait ~10 minutes; Support can confirm the live config via API readback.
comments:
2025-06-10 15:42 UTC — Miguel Santos (Reporter): Customer pinged in shared Slack channel asking why Console still shows max burst GPUs=8 after we raised to 16. They are about to start indexing job. Creating SUP ticket; requesting Console/control plane look.

Customer quote: "We see fewer 429s already, but the Console still says our limit is 8. Can you confirm 16 is actually applied?"

2025-06-10 15:56 UTC — Miguel Santos: Verified via admin tooling that change was applied (audit event emitted). Control plane read API returns updated config. Suspect Console caching or replication lag. Looping in Chloe Martin (Console backend) + Ethan Park (control plane) for quick triage.

2025-06-10 16:12 UTC — Chloe Martin (Assignee): Looking at Console BFF codepath. We cache tenant config in Redis (ttl=3600s) keyed by tenant_id and do not currently invalidate on burst config writes. This would explain up to 60 minutes staleness depending on key creation time.

Next: confirm whether this specific tenant key existed prior to change and when it will expire; consider targeted invalidation.

2025-06-10 16:20 UTC — Ethan Park: Confirmed control plane write path is correct; audit log shows config_change event at 15:37 UTC. No read-replica lag observed (readbacks from primary and replica match new values). Likely Console cache.

Related: we discussed cache invalidation for burst config in #eng-platform when adding Console endpoints; not implemented yet.

2025-06-10 16:33 UTC — Chloe Martin: Found Redis key console:tenant_config:northpeak-prod created earlier today during onboarding checklist walk-through. TTL remaining ~32 minutes at time of report. That matches customer experience.

Mitigation: I can manually delete Redis key for the tenant to unstick immediately while we implement proper invalidation/shorter TTL.
2025-06-10 16:36 UTC — Miguel Santos: OK to purge key. Customer needs visibility before starting job. Please proceed; I’ll message them that Console should update shortly.

2025-06-10 16:41 UTC — Chloe Martin: Deleted tenant key in Redis (eu-west console cache cluster). Customer should see new values after refresh within 1–2 minutes. Also adding a short-term config: reduce TTL to 300s for burst-config subset while we add invalidation hook.

Action item: create follow-up engineering ticket to implement write-through invalidation using audit event stream.

2025-06-10 16:47 UTC — Miguel Santos: Updated customer: "Confirmed limit is active; Console value was cached. Please hard refresh; should show 16 now." Customer confirmed updated limit displayed after refresh.

2025-06-11 09:05 UTC — Chloe Martin: Proposed fix: (1) split burst config into its own cache key with ttl=60s; (2) add invalidation on burst config writes (consume audit event burst.config.updated and purge affected tenant cache).

Also adding last-updated timestamp to API response so UI can display staleness.

Will coordinate with Logan Wright on event consumption patterns. Targeting patch before broad GA enablement in eu-west.

2025-06-11 14:22 UTC — Allison Grant: Please be careful about label/cardinality and avoid per-tenant metrics explosion. For this bug, add a simple counter for cache_hit vs cache_miss on burst-config endpoint + a histogram of config_age_seconds in Console BFF. That helps us detect regressions without per-tenant labels.

2025-06-12 10:11 UTC — Chloe Martin: Patch deployed: burst config cache TTL reduced and invalidation wired off audit event stream in Console BFF. Verified in staging: config updates reflected in UI < 60s.

Notes: if audit event pipeline is delayed, TTL still bounds staleness. Added safe guard to bypass cache when request header X-Force-Refresh is set (internal only) for Support debugging.
2025-06-12 10:25 UTC — Miguel Santos: Customer notified. Asked them to try another small config change (temporary) to confirm propagation. They confirmed UI updated within ~1 minute. Closing ticket.

2025-06-12 10:31 UTC — Miguel Santos: Resolution summary: Console was serving cached tenant config for up to 1 hour without invalidation on burst config writes. Implemented invalidation via burst audit event + reduced TTL for burst config cache keys; added debug refresh header for Support.

Follow-ups: ensure this behavior is covered in GA readiness checklist; update internal onboarding checklist to mention expected propagation (< 5 min) and support workaround if event stream is degraded.
resolution: Fixed in Console BFF: burst config is now cached separately with short TTL and invalidated on burst config write events (audit stream). Support workaround (internal): purge tenant cache key or use force-refresh header. Customer confirmed Console reflects updated limit within ~1 minute post-fix.
customer_visible_next_steps: No action required. If future config changes appear delayed, hard refresh the Console page; Support can confirm live config via control plane readback.
internal_follow_ups: Add regression test that updates burst config and asserts Console API returns new value within 5 minutes.
Update CS onboarding checklist and Support macros to explain propagation expectations and how to validate live config.
